subject.title: feat(durable): persist agent turn front doors

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this durable core runtime and its `durable.mode` authority contract as a supported core product surface, rather than keep durability/recovery work in narrower existing owners or a separately approved roadmap?
rationale: The patch is a broad new core capability with permanent config and persisted-state consequences; implementation tests and a restart trace cannot determine the intended long-term product boundary or operator contract.

options.title: Approve a bounded core durable runtime
options.body: Sponsor the stack direction and require sequential landing with explicit fresh-install, upgrade, disable, and authority-mode recovery proof.

options.title: Narrow to existing owner recovery
options.body: Keep only source-owner-specific recovery improvements and remove the generic durable runtime/config contract from the stack.

options.title: Pause for roadmap design
options.body: Defer the stack until maintainers publish the supported ownership, operator, and persistence boundaries for durable execution.

recommendation.title: Approve a bounded core durable runtime
recommendation.body: Sponsor the stack direction and require sequential landing with explicit fresh-install, upgrade, disable, and authority-mode recovery proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the proposed stack context and can supply the requested scope and compatibility evidence while maintainer sponsorship is obtained.
